# Implement block: Magnify Dock (React Native)

You are adding the "Magnify Dock" block from Native Cook to the user's React Native app. The block already exists as working code. Your job is to bring it into this project faithfully, not to write a new one that looks similar.

## The block

A desktop-style dock of seven invented apps over a blue-hour mountain wallpaper: four ridges fading into the haze under a sky that warms towards a low sun, with the date and a bold "9:41" in the sky. The dock is frosted glass with a lit rim and a soft shadow. Each icon is drawn in layers on a squircle like a real app icon: Postbox (an envelope on blue), Margin (a ruled notepad with a yellow band), Hum (a double note on red), Wayfare (a little map with a river, roads and a pin), Lumen (a camera lens on graphite), Fairweather (a sun behind a cloud) and Workshop (a steel gear). Sliding a finger along the dock swells the icons near it on a smooth falloff, pushing their neighbours apart, with one dark name popover that glides from icon to icon over the one under the finger, resizing to each name as the names cross-fade; a tap launches an app with two bounces and a running dot under it; a long press sets the icons wiggling with a Done button, and an icon can then be dragged to a new place in the row.

**Motion.** Icons are 40 pt at rest, 7 pt apart, inside 8 pt of glass that sits 8 pt above the home indicator with 18 pt corners; each is vector art in a 100-unit box, redrawn at its size so it stays sharp, and the glass is the wallpaper blurred (sigma 18), tinted and rimmed with a top-lit gradient stroke. An icon's scale is 1 + 0.55·(cos(π·d/110) + 1)/2, where d is the distance in pt from its resting centre to the focus (nothing past 110 pt), times how much the dock is magnified; grown icons push everything to their side outward from the dock's centre, the glass widens with them, and if the dock would come within 6 pt of the screen's edges the whole layout is scaled to fit. The focus trails the finger on a critically damped spring (natural frequency 50 rad/s, about 40 ms behind a moving finger) and the magnification swells and settles on another (15 rad/s), letting go when the finger rises more than 120 pt above the dock; both are stepped with their exact solution every frame on the UI thread, so they never jitter at any frame rate. A single name popover (a 28 pt dark pill with a tip) sits 12 pt above the icon under the focus while the dock is more than 30% magnified: it glides to each new icon on a critically damped spring (26 rad/s), resizes to the new name's measured width on the same spring while the names cross-fade with a 90 ms time constant, keeps 8 pt from the screen's edges with its tip still on the icon, and appears and leaves on a 18 rad/s spring, fading, rising 4 pt and growing from 94%. A tap (under 0.4 s, moving under 8 pt) launches the app: it jumps twice, 22 pt then 11 pt high, 0.42 s per jump on a parabola, with a light haptic, and its running dot fades in from 0.35 s. A press held 0.5 s without moving starts editing with a medium haptic: every icon wiggles ±2.4° at 4.2 Hz with a little bob, "Done" fades in at the top right, and the pressed icon is lifted at 1.25× under the finger, following it along the dock and up to 70 pt above it with rubber banding. Once it passes half a slot it takes the new place with a selection haptic and the others spring to their new slots (stiffness 320, damping 30 per unit mass); on release it springs home from where it was dropped, with a light haptic. A tap off the icons or on Done ends editing. The self-playing demo loops every 12 s: a virtual finger lands on Postbox at 0.8 s, slides to Workshop by 3.0 s and back to Hum by 4.2 s, lifts at 4.35 s, taps Hum at 4.95 s to launch it, holds Wayfare from 6.3 s until the dock wiggles, carries it two places right (6.95–7.75 s) and back (8.45–9.25 s), taps Done at 9.95 s, and Hum quits at 10.4 s, its dot fading out. A touch stops the demo for 4 s after the finger lifts; it then ends editing, quits every app, puts the icons back in order and starts over. Under reduced motion the demo does not play, the focus follows the finger without lag, launches show the dot without bouncing, editing does not wiggle and reordered icons jump to their slots.

## Reference source

The block is built and running in the Native Cook source repository. Each link below is a file on GitHub. To read one as plain text, replace `https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/` with `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/` in its address.

## Your instructions

_Anything specific to this app goes here: where the block should appear, what to rename, what to change. Left empty, integrate the block as it is._

## How to work

Work like an experienced React Native engineer joining an existing project: learn the app first, read only what you need, decide early how the block fits, then integrate it with as little disruption as possible. Take the steps in order.

**Done means** the block is reachable in the user's app and behaves like the reference on iOS or Android: a simulator, an emulator or a device. A browser is never proof. Do not open the app on the web to check it, not even when the mobile build fails.

**Fidelity.** Bring over the real implementation. Keep its structure, colours, sizes, timings and easing. Change only what this project requires and what "Your instructions" ask for.

If you already learned this project earlier in the conversation, reuse what you know and skip step 2. Learn it again only if the project changed or something you need is missing.

### 1. Check where you are

- You need the project's files and a terminal. If this prompt was pasted into a chat that has neither, stop and say so: it has to be run by a coding agent opened on the project.
- Confirm the project is a React Native app, Expo or bare. If it is something else, stop, say what you found, and do not create a new app inside it unless the instructions ask for one.

### 2. Learn the host app

- Expo (managed or prebuild) or bare React Native, and the versions of React Native and the Expo SDK.
- The package manager, and how the app is started: Expo Go, a development build, or `react-native run-ios` / `run-android`.
- Navigation: Expo Router, React Navigation, something else, or a single screen. Find how a screen is added today.
- Conventions: TypeScript or not, path aliases, how styles are written, where components and screens live.
- Which of the block's packages are already installed, and at which versions.

### 3. Read the block

- Open the demo, then each file it imports. The list above names every file of the block, so you do not have to guess.
- The demo is how the source repository shows the block. Bring over what the demo renders, not the repository's gallery. Anything listed under "Used by the demo only" stays behind.
- Read the block's props and their defaults. The demo may switch on an option that makes the block play by itself for a recording (for example `autoPlay`). Keep the option; leave it off in the user's app unless asked.

### 4. Decide the fit

- Compare the block's packages with the host's. Install what is missing with the project's own tool (`npx expo install …` in an Expo app, so versions match its SDK).
- A package with native code needs a new native build, and Expo Go only runs the modules it ships with. Say so before you install one, and say which build the user will need.
- If the host is on older versions and an API differs, adapt the block's code to the host. Do not upgrade the host's React Native, Expo SDK or animation libraries without asking.
- Put the files where this app keeps its components. Ask only when two places are equally reasonable and the choice matters.

### 5. Bring it in

- Copy the block's files, keep their names, and rewrite imports to this project's paths and aliases.
- Copy its images and fonts with it, and load fonts the way the project already does.
- Keep reduced-motion handling, haptics and accessibility labels as they are in the source.
- Mount the block where the instructions say. With no instructions, add a screen or route named after the block and make it reachable the way the app's other screens are.

### 6. Run it

- Typecheck and lint with the project's own commands and fix what the block introduced.
- Run the app on the user's usual mobile target and use the block: every state, every gesture, and once with reduced motion on.
- If the simulator, the emulator or the native build fails, report the error and ask how to continue. Do not fall back to the web.

### 7. Report

- Files added and changed, packages installed, and whether a new native build is needed.
- How to reach the block in the app.
- Anything that differs from the reference, and why.
